nn_caretaker.text: Welcome. Shoes off at the door, please, and visitors cover shoulders and knees. It's a working mosque: five prayers a day, and Friday is the busy one.
Look up. Those are Gothic arches, built by French-speaking kings for Christian worship. Now they hold carpets turned towards Mecca. The building has been holy to someone for seven hundred years.
The mihrab, the niche that shows the direction of prayer, was set into the old wall at an angle, because Mecca isn't where the cathedral pointed. You can still see the join.

nn_tourist.text: I came on a day trip from the south. My guidebook calls it Agia Sofia. The sign outside calls it Selimiye. The pigeons don't call it anything. They just live here.
